# 0074: A case may be a scenario with no skill, and its fixtures may be generated, hunted for and promoted

Status: accepted, 2026-10-18.
Extends [0008](0008-evals-are-eval-prefixed-modules.md) (the `@evalcase` contract) and [0044](0044-a-skill-is-invoked-the-way-its-user-invokes-it.md) (a case declares a task), so a case may name no skill.
Extends [0018](0018-fixtures-directory-and-metrics-history.md) (committed fixtures), so a fixture may also be generated.

## Context

Every case invoked a skill, so a command-line tool with no skill could not be measured.
A linter whose findings an agent must clear is the common case.
Every fixture was a committed directory.
A suite that wanted twenty inputs differing only in data committed twenty directories and twenty near-identical case functions.
Nothing searched for an input that breaks the subject.
A failure found by hand had no path back into the suite as a regression.
A record named its skill but not which version of the skill or tool it measured, so two edits of the subject pooled as one.

Prior art shaped each part.
Hypothesis keeps a database of failing examples that it replays first, and `@example` pins one in source.
inspect_ai gives every sample a stable id that a rerun and a log viewer both address.
promptfoo's red team crosses attack plugins with delivery strategies.
AFL keeps a corpus of inputs that found new behaviour and uses a free signal, coverage, to decide which mutants to keep.
Successive halving spends a small budget where earlier rounds looked most promising.

## Decision

**A case that names no skill is a scenario case.** `@evalcase(skill=None)` sends `task` verbatim to every harness through `Harness.prompt`.
No skill is registered with the CLI, and skill coverage and skill use are None.
The **subject** is the directory the suite's `evals/` sits under: the skill, or the tool a scenario exercises.
Records keep the `skill` key as the subject coordinate and add `kind`, either `skill` or `scenario`.

**The subject's version is recorded.** `tracks=` names paths whose content digest is written as `subject_version` on every record.
A tracked path may be absolute or outside the project root, because a tool often lives in its own repository.
A skill case tracks its skill directory, less `evals/`, by default.
A scenario case without `tracks=` records no version.

**A fixture may be a generator.** `fixture=` takes a committed directory name or a `FixtureGenerator`, which yields `Scenario` values.
A scenario is a file map, JSON-able `params`, JSON-able `expect`, and an optional task of its own.
Its id is a readable slug plus a digest of the generator's name, version and canonical params, never a list position.
`params` are what the scenario is, and `expect` are the grader's knobs, such as a recall threshold.
`expect` is kept out of the id, so tuning a tolerance keeps the scenario's history in one piece.
A key may not be both, and the grader reads the two merged as `output.params`.
`Table(expect=[...])` names the row keys that are expectations.
A generated case may declare no `task=` when every scenario names its own, and collection stops on a scenario left with none.
Its fingerprint is the digest of its bytes, recorded so two runs of one id on different bytes never pool.
`Draw` derives its seed from a sha256 digest, never `hash()`, and draws only through `random.Random.random`, whose sequence Python keeps across releases.
The shipped generators are `Table`, `Generated`, `Promoted`, `from_dir` and `Adversarial`.

**Collection expands case by scenario by cell, and stores every scenario.** A node id is `eval_x[<scenario id>/<cell id>]`.
Each scenario is written to `<cache>/scenarios/<suite path>/<case>/<id>/`, with `<id>.provenance.json` beside it, never inside it.
The suite path is the suite file relative to the project root, as records name it.
So two skills' `eval_main.py` never share a store, and the history an adversary reads is keyed the same way.
The cell materialises from there, so the evidence is inspectable and promotable.
A generator that raises, yields nothing, or yields one id twice stops collection by name.
A generator marked `may_be_empty` is the exception for yielding nothing.
`Promoted` before its first promotion and an adversary that found nothing new collect no cells, and collection warns by name.
That warning keeps the silence from reading as a pass.
Every xdist worker collects, so generation and any oracle run once per worker and must be deterministic and process-safe.
The store write is idempotent, staged under a process-unique name and renamed into place.
The provenance file is written last, as the marker of a complete tree.

**An adversarial generator spends a small budget where the subject already breaks.** Each sweep it yields at most `budget` scenarios in three steps.
It confirms, re-running stored past mutants that failed, worst first, up to half the budget.
It explores, drawing new mutants of seed scenarios weighted by `(f + 1) / (n + 2)`, and never re-yields a mutant already sampled or confirmed.
Its draws are salted with a generation, the number of its mutants already sampled, so each sweep explores somewhere new.
A mutant's params are its parent's plus a `mutation` record naming the parent, the mutators, the generation and the attempt.
So the mutant has an id of its own, and its outcomes count toward its parent's weight.
Its `expect` is its parent's.
It screens, keeping a mutant only if a free `oracle` gives it a non-empty signal set new to the sweep.
The outcomes it reads are every stored record of the case, so it is deterministic for a given history and seed.

**Promotion freezes bytes, not parameters.** `python -m pytest_xharness_eval.promote` copies a stored scenario, or the scenario a failed session ran on, into `evals/fixtures/<name>/`.
Its provenance goes beside it, naming the generator, params, fingerprint and the session it came from.
From a session directory, `CacheLayout.holding` finds the cache it sits in, so the command needs no cache argument.
`Promoted` runs every promoted fixture and refuses one whose bytes no longer match their fingerprint.
It is `may_be_empty`, so a suite may declare its regression case before the first failure is promoted.

**A seed is gated before anything spends.** `@evalcase(precheck=...)` takes a function over a `Seed`: the materialised workspace, with any treatment over it, and its scenario.
It raises when the seed no longer sets up what the case is about, such as a linter fixture that no longer trips its rule.
It runs after materialising and before the paid invoke, and a raise errors the cell as a `RunError` with nothing billed and no record written.
Under `--dry-run` the same precheck runs on the same materialised seed, so every fixture is validated for free.

**A record says why a cell did not pass.** `failure` is the first line of what the grader or harness raised, kept to 300 characters.

**A suite's own helper modules import by bare name.** The loader puts the suite's `evals/` directory on `sys.path`, so `_helpers.py` needs no `conftest.py`.

## Consequences

A tool is measured across harness, model, effort and treatment exactly as a skill is, with the same words sent to every arm.
A suite of near-identical directories becomes one case and a table.
A found failure becomes a committed regression in one command, and it stays the same input when its generator changes.

Generation runs at collection, so it is free but repeated on every worker.
A generator whose output changes for the same params must bump `version`, or its records carry one id over two fingerprints.
The adversary's budget is tens of paid runs, not a fuzzer's millions.
Its worth rests on the oracle and the history, and a search with neither is a seeded random walk.

## Lens

An input the subject was measured on must be addressable, reproducible and frozen on demand.
Generate it from code, name it by what made it, keep its bytes, and promote the bytes rather than the recipe.
